title: The Man Who Sold Donkeys
summary: Nasruddin told a buyer: "This donkey has only two faults: when he is grazing, he is hard to catch; and when you catch him, he is no good for anything!"...
full_text:
Nasruddin told a buyer: "This donkey has only two faults: when he is grazing, he is hard to catch; and when you catch him, he is no good for anything!"

The buyer laughed, bought the donkey for a copper, and they remained lifelong friends.
moral: An honest merchant reveals faults beforehand to secure lasting peace.

quiz.question: What fundamental virtue is highlighted in "The Man Who Sold Donkeys"?
options: Foolishness hides wisdom; laughter teaches truth
Acting in hasty anger without listening
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of the story.

quiz.question: How does the central character approach their challenge?
options: Through thoughtful reflection, patience, and presence of mind
By shouting loudly and blaming friends
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in timeless fables.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach readers?
options: Patience, honesty, and humility lead to lasting harmony
quiz.hint: Think about how justice and truth prevail.
